comparison: Strong agreement on E528K mutation mechanism (C8-C10, C88-C93, C133-C135). Both evaluations find the evidence compelling for salt bridge disruption leading to enhanced core disassembly and increased kinase activity. OpenEval provides detailed mechanistic analysis while peer review (Reviewer 3) describes findings as 'compelling evidence' for the allosteric mechanism.

Strong agreement on asciminib mechanism (C11-C12, C113-C115, C119, C130). Both evaluations support the finding that asciminib fixes the αI-helix and prevents type II inhibitor-induced core disassembly. OpenEval emphasizes the mechanical model of force reduction, while peer review describes findings as 'convincing' with asciminib preventing imatinib-induced disassembly.

Strong agreement on αI-helix role and truncation effects (C6-C7, C84, C86-C87, C94-C98, C101, C122, C127). Both evaluations support the systematic truncation experiments and correlations. Peer review describes NMR analysis as 'very clear and convincing' and findings as establishing that truncation results in loss of force on SH2 domain. OpenEval provides detailed quantitative analysis of activity and NMR correlations.

Agreement on foundational background claims (C1-C3, C23, C25-C32, C33-C36, C42-C44). Both evaluations accept these as well-established background knowledge from crystal structures, kinase assays, and prior literature. Peer review acknowledges authors 'previously established' key aspects, while OpenEval categorizes these as foundational regulatory mechanisms.

Complete agreement on background claims about Abl biology, CML pathogenesis, and therapies (C13-C22). Both evaluations accept these as established facts from prior literature. Peer review acknowledges the clinical context and complexity, while OpenEval notes these provide context and identify the knowledge gap motivating the study.

Agreement on methodological context, caveats, and interpretations (C85, C125-C126, C131-C132, C136-C145). Both evaluations accept the experimental limitations (non-phosphorylated constructs, lacking N-cap) and interpretive claims as appropriate scientific qualifications. Peer review notes these reinforce the central role of helix I motions, while OpenEval acknowledges uncertainties appropriately.

Agreement on type II inhibitor-induced core disassembly mechanism (C4-C5, C45-C46, C49, C61-C63, C67-C69, C77-C81, C111-C112). OpenEval provides detailed NMR and PCA analysis, while peer review acknowledges this builds on 'previously published findings' about imatinib-induced disassembly. Both accept the mechanism as established.

Agreement on PCA methodology and results for SH3-SH2 analysis (C65-C66, C70-C76). Peer review describes PCA analysis as 'very clear and convincing' without distinguishing between domains. OpenEval provides detailed methodological assessment including sample sizes and variance explained. Both support the separation of assembled/disassembled states.

Agreement on truncation construct characterization (C51-C58). Peer review (Reviewer 3) acknowledges experimental limitations due to construct instability but states findings are 'sufficient to establish' main conclusions. OpenEval notes progressive reduction in expression yields and correlates with reduced core disassembly. Both accept the data despite limitations.

Partial overlap on quantitative correlations (C94-C98, C127). OpenEval emphasizes strong statistical correlations between kinase activity, NMR-based core disassembly, and structural changes. Peer review supports overall findings as 'convincing' but does not specifically discuss correlation coefficients. Both accept the integrated evidence.

Agreement on unified mechanical model (C105-C110, C116, C118, C120-C121, C123-C124, C128-C129). Peer review explicitly notes work establishes 'a mechanical model of activation' and that results 'reinforce that helix I motions are central to the mechanism.' OpenEval provides detailed analysis of how model integrates all experimental observations including both forces.

Agreement on structural mechanism of force transmission (C102-C104, C99-C100). OpenEval identifies specific structural mechanisms through superposition and NMR analysis, noting some speculation about steric clashes. Peer review implicitly supports through acceptance that truncation 'results in loss of the ability of helix I to impose force on the SH2 domain.'

Agreement on kinase domain PCA analysis (C76-C77, C82-C83). Peer review describes overall PCA analysis as 'very clear and convincing' without separating KD from SH3-SH2 analysis. OpenEval provides detailed assessment of KD-specific PCA including residue coverage and variance explained. Both accept the methodology.

Partial overlap on structural observations and context (C48, C50, C33-C36, C42-C44). Both evaluations accept structural observations from crystal structures and solution NMR as valid context. OpenEval emphasizes conformational differences and flexibility, while peer review accepts these as establishing rationale for the current study.

Agreement on structural background from crystal structures (C33-C36, C42-C44). Both evaluations accept conformational differences, potential clashes, and solution flexibility as well-documented from prior structures. These provide important context for interpreting current NMR results.

Minimal overlap on experimental conditions (C60, C64). Both evaluations acknowledge the NMR experimental setup. OpenEval includes these in broader methodological context discussion, while peer review focuses on PCA methodology without specifically addressing experimental conditions.

Minimal overlap on disease association background (C39-C41). OpenEval includes ABL1 malformation syndrome context in E528K analysis, while peer review groups these with general Abl biology background. Both accept the clinical associations as established.

Minimal overlap on asciminib background (C37-C38). OpenEval includes asciminib introduction in mechanism analysis, while peer review groups with general background. Both accept asciminib as myristate pocket binder.

Minimal overlap on allosteric communication (C125-C126). Both evaluations accept allosteric communication claims based on cited literature. OpenEval includes in broader implications discussion, peer review accepts as part of establishing rationale.

Minimal overlap on knowledge gap (C22). Both evaluations accept this as valid motivation for the study. OpenEval emphasizes it identifies the research gap, peer review accepts it as part of establishing context.
